nota_metodologica: Diferente dos outros 11, Form não é um primitive comportamental do reka-ui — mede volume de glue code de integração vee-validate+zod (schema de validação, estado de erro por campo, submit), não composição de acessibilidade. Ver metrics/complexity-ranking-predicted.md.

supports keyboard-only submission (Tab through fields, Enter to submit)
testes.nota: 2 of 5 failed on the first try: (1) the schema's plain z.string().email(...) message only applies to the format check, not the empty/undefined case, which falls back to zod's generic 'Required' — fixed by adding explicit required_error messages; (2) 'submits valid values' failed because vee-validate's handleSubmit validates asynchronously even against a synchronous zod schema — the emit lands a tick after the click, confirmed by isolating a raw form (no vee-validate) where the same click->emit pattern was synchronous. Needed an explicit waitFor(), not just `await user.click`.

ds_shadcn.vantagem_real_do_pronto:
This is the one component where the CLI-generated code provides something ds-reka has to hand-roll from scratch: FormControl auto-wires aria-describedby/aria-invalid between the input and its error message via useFormField's generated ids (formItemId/formDescriptionId/formMessageId) — ds-reka's LoginForm has no equivalent wiring (its error

is just visually adjacent to the input, not aria-linked to it). That's a real accessibility gap in the ds-reka version this round didn't need to close to pass its own test suite (axe didn't flag it, since a visually-adjacent error text isn't itself a violation), but it's a genuine, measurable difference in how complete the two versions are.
